hero.title: Saffron Hearth — Old City: Website & Online Presence Report
hero.subtitle: Strong food, soft digital footprint. Here's where the money is leaking.
narrative: Saffron Hearth has built a loyal following in Old City around handmade naan, slow-braised lamb, and a saffron rice that regulars order by name. The food is doing its job. The internet, less so.

Your Google listing is missing photos that match what walks out the kitchen door, the website ranks for almost nothing beyond your brand name, and a handful of nearby Indian and Mediterranean restaurants are quietly pulling search traffic that should be yours.

This report walks through what we found in three buckets — your Google Business Profile, your website, and the paid-ad opportunity once the first two are in shape. Each section ends with the specific moves we'd make first.
hero.verdict: Beloved Old City neighborhood spot, weak digital presence holding back new-customer flow.

sections.title: Website
sections.intro: Your website's job is to convert the people who land on it — and to bring in new ones from search. Right now it does neither well. Both are fixable with the same set of changes.

sections.title: What's Holding Your Website Back
sections.intro: Five specific issues are doing most of the damage. Each one is a one-day fix on its own; together they shift the site from 'invisible' to 'finding new customers every week.'

items.title: The homepage doesn't say what you cook or where you cook it
body: Saffron Hearth's homepage opens with a hero image of a candle and the headline 'A Warm Place.' Beautiful, but a stranger landing from Google has no idea this is an Indian restaurant in Old City Philadelphia until they scroll halfway down the page.
Google reads pages the same way humans skim them. If the first 200 words don't mention 'Indian,' 'Old City,' or 'Philadelphia,' the site has no business showing up for those searches.
bullets: Rewrite the hero headline to include cuisine + neighborhood.
Add a short intro paragraph above the fold mentioning Old City and the dishes you're known for.
Move the menu link to the top of the navigation.

items.title: No dedicated pages for the dishes you're known for
body: Customers search 'best naan philadelphia,' 'lamb biryani near me,' and 'saffron rice old city' every month. Your site has a single Menu page that's a PDF, which Google can't fully read and customers can't easily share.
Each signature dish should have its own page with a paragraph, a photo, and a price. Three dish pages can pull more search traffic in 90 days than a single Menu page has in two years.

items.title: No catering page
body: Catering is the highest-margin order any restaurant on this block can take. Olive Branch ranks #1 for 'old city catering' with one mediocre page. Saffron Hearth has nothing.

A 600-word catering page with a sample menu, pricing tiers, and a contact form is a one-day build. Based on neighborhood search volume, it should bring 2–4 catering inquiries per month within a quarter.

items.title: The site is slow on phone, especially on the menu
body: Largest Contentful Paint on the menu page is 4.8 seconds on a 4G connection. Anything past 2.5s and Google deprioritizes you in mobile search. Most of the load is from a 3.4MB hero image and an unoptimized PDF.
Converting the menu PDF to a real HTML page (which we recommended above for other reasons) also cuts the page weight by ~80%.

items.title: No reviews surfaced on the site
body: You have a 4.7★ average — the highest in the area — and the site shows none of it. A short rotating quote block with three customer reviews and a star count is one of the highest-converting elements you can add to a restaurant homepage.
Pulling those quotes from your existing Google reviews is a 30-minute job.

totals.summary: **Where you stand today vs. where you can be in 3 months:** saffronhearth.example is currently pulling roughly **80–150 visitors a month** — almost all of them branded searches for the restaurant by name. With the keyword set above rolled out across the site and GBP, plus three new dish pages and a catering page, a realistic **3-month target is 800+ monthly visitors**, growing toward 1,500+ by month six — roughly a **8–10× lift**. On a 4,200–6,900 monthly-search opportunity across the four groups, that's comfortably within reach at a 5–8% capture rate.

sections.title: Google Ads
sections.intro: Once the website and GBP fixes above are in place, a small monthly ad budget compounds the lift instead of papering over the gaps. Here's what a realistic 90-day ad spend looks like for Old City.

sections.title: Ad Spend & Estimated Returns
sections.intro: Old City is mid-competition for restaurant ads — CPCs sit around $2.40–$4.50 on the money-keywords cluster. Assumes ~10–12% click-to-call/order conversion and a $32 average ticket. Numbers are conservative because direct orders skip the 20–30% delivery-app commission.
sections.callout: **How to read this.** The ads target your highest-intent searches ('indian food old city,' 'lamb curry near me,' 'indian catering old city,' plus your secret-weapon dish terms). Conversion sits around 10–12% of clicks turning into a call or direct order. Average ticket is ~$32 dine-in / pickup, higher on catering. ROAS is reported conservatively — once catering inquiries are factored in (each one $500+), the Growth tier typically clears 2–3× by month three. **Start with Growth.** It's the spend tier where the math holds even in a slow month, and it's where most Old City competitors land too.

sections.title: The path from here
sections.intro: Four steps, in order. Each one builds on the last.

steps.label: Research Competition & Keywords
steps.info: Map who's winning in Old City and the exact searches your customers use, before any work begins.

steps.label: Optimize Google Business Profile
steps.info: Fix categories, photos, menu, hours, and Q&A so Google ranks you in the top 3 for local searches.

steps.label: SEO Optimized Website
steps.info: Rebuild the homepage, dish pages, and catering page so search engines and customers both find what they need fast.

steps.label: Google Ads
steps.info: Once GBP and the site are in shape, paid ads compound the lift — only worth running after the first three steps.

sections.title: Investment & Next Steps
body: Saffron Hearth — Old City has the food, the rating, and the neighborhood loyalty that most restaurants spend years trying to build. What's missing is the digital surface area that turns all of that into a steady flow of new customers.

The plan above is sequenced so each step makes the next one work harder. The GBP fixes are immediate and low cost. The website work is a 4–6 week project. The ad spend only kicks in once the first two are doing their job — which is the difference between paying for clicks that convert and paying for clicks that bounce.
When you're ready, we'll walk through the scope, the timeline, and exactly which pieces our team handles versus which ones we set up for your team to own going forward.
